paragraphs.source_en: “...Thus, what we call public morality is extremely important. I have been abroad, and whether in France, Germany, or England, wherever one goes, there is no country where public morality is not practiced. Moreover, no matter how lowly a person may be, there is no one who does not attach importance to public morality. Sadly, in this respect we Japanese cannot compare with foreign countries. Among you gentlemen, when public morality is mentioned, some may perhaps think it is something new imported from abroad. In fact, to think so is a grave mistake. The ancients, too, said: ‘The Master's Way is bound together by one thread: loyalty and consideration, that is all.’ This character ‘shu,’ in other words, is precisely the source from which public morality arises. I too am human, and at times I feel like singing loudly. But when I am reading and hear someone in the next room singing at the top of his voice, I can no longer go on reading. Therefore, even when I myself would like to recite selections from Tang poetry aloud and relieve my spirits, if there is someone in the neighboring room who, like me, cannot bear noise, I feel I would be wronging him. In such circumstances, I always restrain myself. I hope that you gentlemen, too, will observe public morality as far as possible, and that whatever you think may hinder others you will firmly refrain from doing...”

paragraphs.source_en: The master inclined his ear and listened intently to this discourse. When he heard this final sentence, he could not help giving a faint smile. Here I must offer a brief explanation of that ‘faint smile.’ A cynic reading this might well suppose that there was a note of sarcasm in it. But my master is by no means such a harsh man. Rather than call him harsh toward others, it would be more accurate to say that his intelligence is not especially developed. As for why the master laughed, it was entirely because he was pleased. Since a teacher of ethics had admonished his students so earnestly, surely from then on he would no longer be subjected to attacks by Dum-Dum bullets. That being so, for a good while at least, his head would not go bald. Even if his hot-headed symptoms could not be cured at once, once the proper time came they would gradually recover. Having judged that he would no longer need to put a wet towel on his head and thrust his feet into the kotatsu, nor worry about sleeping out under trees and on stones, he smiled faintly. For a master who, even today in the twentieth century, still honestly believes that borrowed money must always be repaid, it was only natural that he should listen to the other teacher's discourse in all seriousness.

paragraphs.source_zh: 主人侧着耳朵聚精会神地听着这番讲话。当他听到最后这句话时，不由得微微一笑。这里，我得对这“微微一笑”稍作解释。一个玩世家读到这里，很可能认为这里边含有讥讽的意味。但是我家主人决不是那样苛刻的人。与其说他待人苛刻，还不如说他是一个智慧不太发达的人。说到主人为什么发笑，这完全是由于他感到高兴而笑。一个做伦理教师的人，既然这样痛切地训诫他的学生，那么肯定今后他再也不会遭受达姆达姆弹的袭击了。这样，在相当一段时间内，他的头也不致变秃了。虚火上升的症状即使一时不能痊愈，只要到了一定时候，也会逐渐恢复的。由于他断定以后再也不用拿湿手巾顶在头上，两脚伸进被炉里去，也不用担心要在树下石上露宿了，所以他才微微一笑。在二十世纪的今天，仍然正直地认为借钱一定要还的主人，当然会以老老实实的态度来倾听对方教师的这番讲话的。

paragraphs.source_en: Before long, it seemed that class time had ended, and the ethics teacher's lecture suddenly stopped. The lessons in the other classrooms all ended at the same moment. Then the eight hundred brave fellows who had until then been tightly sealed inside the classrooms raised a great shout and rushed out of the building; their force was exactly like a large hornets' nest more than a foot long being knocked down. Buzzing and bawling all together, they leapt out from windows, sliding doors, hinged doors, and any hole whatever through which they could squeeze, each trying to get ahead, without the slightest pause. This was the beginning of the great incident.

paragraphs.source_zh: 过不多久，似乎到了下课的时间，那位伦理教师的讲话戛然而止。其他教室里的授课也同时结束了。于是刚才还紧紧关在教室里的八百位好汉，一下子哇地高喊着，从建筑物里飞跑出来，那种气势，和捅掉一尺多长的大马蜂窝毫无两样。他们一起嗡嗡、哇哇地叫喊着，从窗子、拉门、能开阖的小门，还有只要能够钻出去的窟窿里争先恐后、毫不停留地蹦了出去。这就是大事件的开端。
